problem:
The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. Given that $Y∼N(5,{4}^{2}),$ compute $P(Y\ge 7.84).$ Use the table below and do not round your answer.

| $z$ | $\,0.00\,$ | $\,0.01\,$ | $\,0.02\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,0.7\,$ | $\,0.7580\,$ | $\,0.7611\,$ | $\,0.7642\,$ |
| $\,0.8\,$ | $\,0.7881\,$ | $\,0.7910\,$ | $\,0.7939\,$ |
| $\,0.9\,$ | $\,0.8159\,$ | $\,0.8186\,$ | $\,0.8212\,$ |

$P(Y\ge 7.84)=$
{{field-1}}
worked_solution:
Given a normal random variable $Y∼N(\mu ,{\sigma }^{2}),$ we have

$$
P(Y\ge y)=P(Z\ge \frac{y-\mu }{\sigma })
$$

where $Z∼N(0,1)$ is a standard normal random variable. In our case, we have $\mu =5$ and $\sigma =4.$

First, we transform $Y$ into a standard normal random variable $Z$ by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Y\ge 7.84) & =P(Z\ge \frac{7.84-5}{4}) \\  & =P\,(Z\ge \frac{2.84}{4}) \\  & =P(Z\ge 0.71)\end{aligned}
$$

The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14070250/assets/a5bf63797840ba4b457ef4f8564b979e106fa916b2247937733157830d6f443d.png)

Now, we express the required probability in terms of $Φ(z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Z\ge 0.71) & =1-P(Z<0.71) \\  & =1-P(Z\le 0.71) \\  & =1-Φ(0.71)\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, we know that

$$
Φ(0.71)=0.7611.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Z\ge 0.71) & =1-0.7611 \\  & =0.2389.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we conclude that

$$
P(Y\ge 7.84)=0.2389.
$$
